collection_mechanisms.mechanism_details: Adult data were collected using the custom Bridge2AI-Voice application running on a tablet, which hosts the acoustic task protocol, demographic surveys, confounder questions and validated questionnaires.
Pediatric data were collected using reproschema-ui with the Bridge2AI-Voice pediatric protocol.
Questionnaire and clinical validation data were captured in and exported from REDCap; the supporting REDCap data dictionary, metadata and instrument PDFs are published separately.

Recording hardware comprised iPads (9th or 10th generation) and iPad Air (5th generation) with an Avid AE-36 microphone connected through an Apple dongle; a head-mounted headset with microphone was used where possible, though the microphone could sit at slightly different distances between recordings.

d4d_fields.description: The Bridge2AI-Voice adult dataset is a large, ethically sourced and demographically diverse collection of voice, speech, breathing and cough data linked to health information, generated by the Bridge2AI-Voice consortium under the NIH Common Fund Bridge2AI program. Participants were recruited at high-volume expert clinics at academic institutions in the United States and Canada on the basis of membership in five disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders - together with controls. Each participant completed a standardized protocol of acoustic tasks recorded on a tablet application, self-reported demographic and medical history questionnaires, disease-specific validated questionnaires, and clinician-performed gold standard diagnostic validation. Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 participants across five North American sites. The public release contains data considered low risk: derivations of the audio such as spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, pitch contours, articulatory features, phonetic posteriorgrams and static acoustic features, distributed as Apache Parquet files, alongside phenotype tables and per-recording metadata distributed as tab-separated values with accompanying JSON data dictionaries. The original voice recordings are not part of the public release and are disseminated only through controlled access. The consortium's stated flagship target is a dataset of 10,000 voices linked to health information. The consortium publishes a self-assessment of the dataset against the Bridge2AI AI-readiness recommendations, in which the dataset scores 100 percent on FAIRness (findable, accessible, interoperable, reusable), 100 percent on provenance (transparent, traceable, interpretable, key actors identified), 80 percent on characterization, 100 percent on pre-model explainability, 100 percent on ethics (ethically acquired, managed, disseminated and secure), 50 percent on sustainability, and 75 percent on computability.

irb_approval: Data collection and sharing were approved by the University of South Florida Institutional Review Board. The protocol was submitted to and approved by the USF single IRB, and subsite IRBs were engaged through the single IRB process.
human_subject_research.ethics_review_board: University of South Florida Institutional Review Board, acting as single IRB for the United States sites; the Research Ethics Board at the Hospital for Sick Children for the pediatric cohort; Canadian participating institutions applied for separate research ethics board approvals in accordance with Canadian regulations.
regulatory_compliance: HIPAA de-identification rules are applied to the released data, and study data are hosted on infrastructure operated by NIH STRIDES partners that hold pre-negotiated agreements with the NIH for data privacy and HIPAA protection. The study is not a drug study and is not a medical device study, and no data monitoring committee was appointed.
special_populations: Pediatric participants aged 2 to 18 were recruited only at the Hospital for Sick Children and are released as the separate Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset.

related_datasets.name: Bridge2AI-Voice Pediatric Dataset
related_datasets.description: The companion pediatric release, collected at the Hospital for Sick Children under a separate Research Ethics Board approval and the Bridge2AI-Voice pediatric protocol. Version 1.1.0 contains derived audio features for 23,533 recordings collected from 300 participants aged 2 to 18. The DOI 10.13026/mf9s-5r03 resolves to the latest version of the pediatric dataset.

related_datasets.name: Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information (version 1.0)
related_datasets.description: The first release of the feature-only dataset, version 1.0, published on the Health Data Nexus, which provides cloud compute alongside the dataset rather than allowing data downloads.

subpopulations.identification: Demographic sub-populations are identified by age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status in the demographics table.
subpopulations.distribution: The dataset has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors; groups that have less trust in the medical system or in AI, or that are less proximal to the collection sites, would have been less likely to be recruited.

subpopulations.identification: Participants are grouped into five disease cohort categories - voice disorders, neurological and neurodegenerative disorders, mood and psychiatric disorders, respiratory disorders, and pediatric voice and speech disorders - together with control participants who do not have the conditions of interest.
subpopulations.distribution: The public data releases do not contain an equal distribution of these disease categories; the initial release contained data from four of the five categories, and the adult dataset contains adult participants only.
